**UK launches consultation on next-generation retail payments infrastructure**

*The Retail Payments Infrastructure Board has opened a consultation on the design of the UK's future retail payment system, the most significant structural review since the New Payments Architecture was shelved.*

The Bank of England-led RPIB published its consultation on June 25, inviting industry input on the architecture that will eventually replace the UK's existing Faster Payments and Bacs systems. The consultation follows the RPIB's November 2025 strategy paper and sits within the broader National Payments Vision framework overseen by HM Treasury, the FCA and the Payment Systems Regulator.

Pay.UK will continue to operate existing systems during the transition, but the consultation signals that the UK is now actively scoping a replacement rather than iterating on what exists. The design choices made here will shape how variable recurring payments, open banking-initiated transfers and overlay services such as confirmation of payee operate for the next decade or more.

The consultation arrives at a moment when the UK is simultaneously launching its new domestic card scheme (UKPI), implementing commercial VRPs and absorbing the SEPA instant payments mandate's implications for cross-border interoperability. How the next-generation infrastructure accommodates these parallel initiatives will determine whether the UK payments landscape simplifies or fragments further.

*Sources: [The Retail Payments Infrastructure Board launches consultation on the next generation UK payments infrastructure](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/news/2026/june/rpib-launches-consultation-on-next-generation-uk-payments-infrastructure) — Bank of England | [RPIB Consults on UK's Next-Generation Payments System](https://www.finance-monthly.com/rpib-consultation-uk-next-generation-payments-infrastructure/) — Finance Monthly | [UK's Retail Payments Infrastructure Board launches consultation](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47997/uks-retail-payments-infrastructure-board-launches-consultation) — Finextra*

**Bank of England drops individual holding caps in stablecoin regulatory rethink**

*The BoE has revised its approach to stablecoin regulation, removing proposed individual holding limits in a policy statement that clears a path toward a 2027 supervisory regime.*

The Bank of England's updated policy statement abandons the individual holding caps it had previously consulted on for sterling-denominated stablecoins. The original proposal would have limited how much any single person could hold in a regulated stablecoin, a constraint that the industry argued would cripple utility for payments and treasury use cases alike.

By removing the cap, the BoE is signalling a more permissive stance that aligns stablecoin regulation more closely with how electronic money is already treated. The 2027 target date for the full supervisory framework gives issuers and payment firms a clearer timeline for product development and licensing applications.

The shift comes as stablecoin payment rails gain traction across European infrastructure. Mastercard recently added stablecoin settlement to its merchant network, ClearBank Europe launched digital asset rails with SEPA instant payouts, and multiple eurozone initiatives are exploring tokenised money alongside the digital euro. The BoE's willingness to ease its initial constraints suggests UK regulators want to remain competitive in this space rather than let restrictive rules push activity offshore.

*Sources: [Bank of England drops individual holding caps in stablecoin rule rethink for 2027](https://www.globalgovernmentfinance.com/bank-of-england-stablecoins-policy-statement/) — Global Government Finance*

**Airwallex reaches $11 billion valuation with $320 million raise targeting agentic commerce**

*Airwallex has raised $320 million at an $11 billion valuation, positioning the cross-border payments firm for a push into autonomous finance and AI-agent-initiated transactions.*

The funding round marks a substantial step up for Airwallex, which acquired reconciliation platform Leapfin earlier this month as part of a broader build-out of its infrastructure for cross-border merchants. The $11 billion valuation places it among the most highly valued private payments companies globally.

Airwallex's stated focus on agentic commerce reflects a pattern emerging across the payments industry. Visa has partnered with OpenAI, ING completed Europe's first agentic payment with Worldline and Mastercard, and Stripe has built a payment layer for AI agents. Airwallex is betting that cross-border business payments, where complexity and manual processes remain significant, are particularly suited to autonomous execution.

The raise also positions Airwallex for a potential public listing, though the company has not confirmed timing. With Nuvei in advanced talks to acquire Payoneer and OpenPayd pursuing a Nasdaq listing via SPAC, the cross-border payments sector is entering a phase of consolidation and capital markets activity that will reshape the competitive landscape.

*Sources: [Airwallex targets agentic commerce after hitting $11bn valuation](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/47996/airwallex-targets-agentic-commerce-after-hitting-11bn-valuation) — Finextra*

**FCA confirms BNPL regulation begins July 15 with new consumer protections**

*The FCA will begin regulating buy now, pay later products from July 15, bringing mandatory affordability checks and complaints rights to a market that has operated largely outside the regulatory perimeter.*

The FCA published a blog post on June 25 setting out its case for the new rules, confirming the July 15 start date for BNPL regulation. From that date, BNPL providers will need to conduct affordability assessments, give consumers access to the Financial Ombudsman Service and meet FCA standards on marketing and pre-contractual information.

The timing is notable given TrueLayer's recent acquisition of a Dutch BNPL firm to add credit at checkout. Open banking-powered affordability checks are increasingly positioned as the mechanism through which BNPL providers can meet regulatory requirements efficiently, using real-time income and spending data rather than static credit bureau records. The FCA's earlier signals that open banking data would reshape mortgage affordability checks point in the same direction.

For payment firms and open banking providers, the regulatory start date creates immediate commercial demand for compliant data-sharing and verification services. Providers that cannot demonstrate adequate affordability checks by mid-July face enforcement risk in a market the FCA has flagged as a consumer protection priority.

*Sources: [Why stronger Buy Now Pay Later protections are the right step for consumers](https://www.fca.org.uk/news/blogs/why-stronger-buy-now-pay-later-protections-are-right-step-consumers) — FCA*
